```{r libraries, message = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261125)
```

## The paper

Alidori *et al.* (2017), *PLoS One* **12**(8):e0183902,
[doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0183902](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0183902),
report the *in vivo* pharmacology of an ammonium-functionalized single-walled
carbon nanotube (fCNT), tracer-radiolabelled with yttrium-86 ([86Y]fCNT) and
imaged by dynamic whole-body PET/CT in two healthy male cynomolgus monkeys
(*Macaca fascicularis*). The radiolabel rapidly clears the blood (blood
t<sub>1/2</sub> ~ 7 min) and accumulates in the kidney cortex and liver before
intact urinary elimination.

The quantitative modelling is a pair of **linear two-compartment tissue models,
one per organ, driven by a measured whole-blood input forcing function** (the
mean activity in a heart volume-of-interest). These were fitted with the SAAM II
software:

* **Kidney** -- a *serial* (catenary) topology (Fig 3A): blood feeds the renal
  tissue space (C1), which either eliminates tracer into urine or resorbs it
  into a proximal-tubule-cell hold-up sink (C2) that slowly returns it.
* **Liver** -- a *parallel* (mammillary) topology (Fig 4A): blood feeds the
  hepatic tissue (C1) and the liver sinusoidal endothelium (C2) independently,
  each with its own loss route back to blood or into bile.

Both fits held the organ blood-volume fraction fixed (15% kidney, 20% liver).
This article reproduces the two packaged models, traces every rate constant to
the source, and shows the structural behaviour the models predict. Because the
models are deterministic typical-value fits over two animals, there is no
population simulation / NCA step; the validation is structural (the C1/C2
decomposition the paper plots in Figs 3C and 4C) plus a terminal-half-life
forensic.

```{r models}
kidney <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Alidori_2017_fCNT_kidney_cyno"))
liver <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Alidori_2017_fCNT_liver_cyno"))
```

* Kidney description: `r kidney$description`
* Liver description: `r liver$description`

## Population

Two healthy male cynomolgus monkeys (Charles River), 3.5 years old, 3.2-4.5 kg
at dosing (Table 3), each given a single IV injection of 5 mg (5 MBq, 0.135 mCi)
[86Y]fCNT (~ 1 mg/kg) and imaged for a 3-hour dynamic PET/CT protocol
immediately after injection. Animal 1 was followed for 6 months, Animal 2 for
2 weeks. A correlative mouse tissue-harvest biodistribution study in the same
paper was not fitted with a compartmental model and is not packaged here.

## Source trace

Every fitted rate constant is held `fixed()` in the packaged models; the organ
blood-volume fraction is a fixed structural constant. The values below are the
Supporting Information table values (four significant figures), which match the
rounded values printed in the Fig 3B / Fig 4B tables.

```{r sourcetrace, echo = FALSE}
st <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Organ,    ~Symbol, ~Meaning,                                      ~Value,   ~Source,
  "Kidney",  "k1",    "blood -> kidney uptake (1/min)",              0.93922,  "S1 Table; Fig 3B = 0.939",
  "Kidney",  "k2",    "kidney -> urine elimination (1/min)",         0.15439,  "S1 Table; Fig 3B = 0.154",
  "Kidney",  "k3",    "kidney -> proximal-tubule-cell sink (1/min)", 0.02875,  "S1 Table; Fig 3B = 0.0289",
  "Kidney",  "k4",    "tubule-cell sink -> kidney return (1/min)",   0.00382,  "S1 Table; Fig 3B = 0.00382",
  "Kidney",  "fvb",   "renal blood-volume fraction",                 0.15,     "S1 Table caption (fixed)",
  "Liver",   "k1",    "blood -> liver C1 uptake (1/min)",            0.21158,  "S2 Table; Fig 4B = 0.211",
  "Liver",   "k2",    "liver C1 -> blood/bile loss (1/min)",         0.41722,  "S2 Table; Fig 4B = 0.417",
  "Liver",   "k3",    "blood -> sinusoidal endothelium (1/min)",     0.01003,  "S2 Table; Fig 4B = 0.0100",
  "Liver",   "k4",    "sinusoidal endothelium -> loss (1/min)",      0.00319,  "S2 Table; Fig 4B = 0.00319",
  "Liver",   "fvb",   "hepatic blood-volume fraction",               0.20,     "S2 Table caption (fixed)"
)
knitr::kable(st)
```

The Supporting Information tables also report the standard deviation, %CV and
95% CI of each rate constant (parameter uncertainty of the deterministic
two-animal fit, *not* between-subject variability): kidney k1-k4 at 7.0 / 14.5 /
13.2 / 17.9 %CV; liver k1-k4 at 14.2 / 14.6 / 3.8 / 11.2 %CV.

## The blood input forcing function

Both models read the whole-blood activity curve as a time-varying regressor
`SUV_BLOOD` (declared `linear(SUV_BLOOD)` so `rxode2` interpolates linearly
between rows). The paper derived this curve from the heart VOI but **does not
tabulate it**, so for this illustration we use a representative blood profile:
a fast bi-exponential dominated by the reported ~ 7-minute blood half-life plus
a small slow tail. Users with their own PET data should supply the measured
heart-VOI SUV curve through `SUV_BLOOD`.

```{r bloodinput}
# Representative whole-blood SUV input over the 195-minute scan window.
# Fast phase: blood t1/2 ~ 7 min (Alidori 2017, "Rapid blood compartment
# clearance was observed (t1/2 ~ 7 min)"). Illustrative amplitude only.
tgrid <- c(seq(0, 10, by = 0.25), seq(11, 195, by = 1))
blood_suv <- 7 * exp(-log(2) / 7 * tgrid) + 0.6 * exp(-log(2) / 90 * tgrid)
blood <- data.frame(time = tgrid, SUV_BLOOD = blood_suv)

ggplot(blood, aes(time, SUV_BLOOD)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#b8860b") +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Whole-blood SUV (illustrative)") +
  theme_bw()
```

## Structural behaviour: the C1 / C2 decomposition (Figs 3C and 4C)

The characteristic signature of both organ models -- independent of the blood
input's absolute scale -- is that the deep hold-up compartment (C2) fills slowly
and overtakes the fast tissue compartment (C1) within the first hour, producing
the sustained tissue plateau the paper plots in Figs 3C (kidney) and 4C (liver).
We solve the typical-value models (`zeroRe()`) under the representative blood
input and reproduce that decomposition.

```{r solve}
solve_organ <- function(mod, c1, c2, dose_cmt) {
  ev <- data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = blood$time, evid = 0L,
    cmt = dose_cmt, SUV_BLOOD = blood$SUV_BLOOD
  )
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  tibble::tibble(
    time = s$time,
    total = s$Cc,
    C1 = s[[c1]],
    C2 = s[[c2]]
  )
}

kid <- solve_organ(kidney, "kidney", "kidney_ptc", "kidney")
liv <- solve_organ(liver, "liver", "liver_lsec", "liver")
```

```{r fig3c, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Kidney tissue SUV and its C1 / C2 decomposition (reproduces the shape of Alidori 2017 Fig 3C)."}
kid |>
  pivot_longer(c(total, C1, C2), names_to = "curve", values_to = "SUV") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, SUV, colour = curve)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(total = "forestgreen", C1 = "red", C2 = "blue"),
    labels = c(total = "total kidney", C1 = "C1 (renal tissue)", C2 = "C2 (tubule-cell sink)")
  ) +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Kidney SUV", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig4c, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Liver tissue SUV and its C1 / C2 decomposition (reproduces the shape of Alidori 2017 Fig 4C)."}
liv |>
  pivot_longer(c(total, C1, C2), names_to = "curve", values_to = "SUV") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, SUV, colour = curve)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(total = "forestgreen", C1 = "red", C2 = "blue"),
    labels = c(total = "total liver", C1 = "C1 (hepatic tissue)", C2 = "C2 (sinusoidal endothelium)")
  ) +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Liver SUV", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r crossover}
# C2 overtakes C1 within the first hour in both organs (the paper's Figs 3C/4C
# cross-over), and the deep sink then governs the plateau.
kid_cross <- kid$time[which(kid$C2 > kid$C1)[1]]
liv_cross <- liv$time[which(liv$C2 > liv$C1)[1]]
c(kidney_crossover_min = kid_cross, liver_crossover_min = liv_cross)

stopifnot(
  # Both deep compartments overtake their fast compartment inside the first hour.
  kid_cross > 0, kid_cross < 60,
  liv_cross > 0, liv_cross < 60,
  # Tissue signal is sustained: the kidney total is still a large fraction of its
  # peak at the end of the 195-min scan (the renal-cell sink, Fig 3C plateau).
  max(kid$total) > 0,
  kid$total[nrow(kid)] > 0.4 * max(kid$total)
)
```

## Terminal half-life forensic

Once the blood input has cleared, each model decays by its own slowest
eigenvalue. For the **serial kidney** model the two-state loss matrix is

$$ \begin{pmatrix} -(k_2+k_3) & k_4 \\ k_3 & -k_4 \end{pmatrix}, $$

and for the **parallel liver** model the two compartments decay independently at
$k_2$ (fast tissue) and $k_4$ (slow sinusoidal endothelium).

```{r halflife}
kp <- as.list(stats::setNames(kidney$theta, names(kidney$theta)))
lp <- as.list(stats::setNames(liver$theta, names(liver$theta)))

# Kidney: slowest eigenvalue of the serial loss matrix.
A_kid <- matrix(c(-(kp$kelim + kp$kseq), kp$kret,
                  kp$kseq, -kp$kret), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
lam_kid <- max(Re(eigen(A_kid)$values)) # slowest (least negative) rate, 1/min
t_half_kid <- log(2) / -lam_kid / 60 # hours

# Liver: parallel model, slow compartment governs the terminal phase.
t_half_liv <- log(2) / lp$kret / 60 # hours

c(kidney_terminal_t_half_h = round(t_half_kid, 2),
  liver_terminal_t_half_h = round(t_half_liv, 2))
```

```{r halflife_check}
# The printed rate constants give a terminal half-life near 3.6 h for both
# organs -- NOT the 11.9 h reported in the abstract / Figs 3D & 4D legends.
stopifnot(
  abs(t_half_kid - 3.6) < 0.3,
  abs(t_half_liv - 3.6) < 0.3
)
```

The four-parameter organ models, with the published rate constants, reproduce
the **measured** 0-195 min window (Figs 3C/4C above). They do **not** reproduce
the ~ 11.9 h "biological half-life" or the 72-hour extrapolations in Figs 3D and
4D: those require the whole-blood input to be carried as a slowly-declining tail
far beyond the 195-minute scan (the organs track the slow whole-body blood
activity, whose intrinsic clearance is slower than either organ's own
eigenvalue). The blood tail beyond the scan is not tabulated and is not part of
the packaged tissue model. Digitising the kidney curve in Fig 3D gives a
terminal half-life of ~ 11 h, consistent with the stated 11.9 h and with a
sustained blood tail rather than the ~ 3.6 h organ eigenvalue. See the
Assumptions and deviations section.

## Flux / mass-balance sanity

At the C1/C2 cross-over the two compartments approach a pseudo-equilibrium in
which the sequestration flux into the sink is close to the return flux out of
it. For the kidney sink this is `k3 * C1` in versus `k4 * C2` out; because
`k3 >> k4`, the sink concentrates tracer (C2 > C1), exactly as the paper notes
("the rate constant describing loss ... (k4) is an order of magnitude smaller
than the entrance rate constant (k3)").

```{r flux}
# Ratio of sink entrance to exit rate constants (both organs): entrance >> exit,
# so the deep compartment accumulates. Paper: k3 an order of magnitude > k4.
c(kidney_k3_over_k4 = round(kp$kseq / kp$kret, 1),
  liver_k3_over_k4 = round(lp$kseq / lp$kret, 1))

stopifnot(
  kp$kseq / kp$kret > 5, # kidney sink entrance >> exit
  lp$kseq / lp$kret > 2  # liver sink entrance > exit
)
```

## Assumptions and deviations

* **Species.** Preclinical model; `population$species = "cynomolgus monkey
  (Macaca fascicularis)"`. The `description` of each packaged model is prefixed
  "Preclinical (cynomolgus monkey)".
* **Drug.** The agent is a tracer-radiolabelled ammonium-functionalized
  single-walled carbon nanotube ([86Y]fCNT); there is no INN. The file stem uses
  `fCNT`.
* **Two models, one paper.** The kidney (serial) and liver (parallel) models are
  independent SAAM II fits with different topologies, packaged as two files
  (`Alidori_2017_fCNT_kidney_cyno`, `Alidori_2017_fCNT_liver_cyno`) and this one
  vignette.
* **Observation output `Cc`.** Each model's single output is the organ VOI
  standardized uptake value (SUV), named `Cc` per the single-output convention
  with `units$concentration = "SUV"`. There is no plasma central compartment;
  `Cc = fvb * SUV_BLOOD + C1 + C2`, i.e. a fixed blood-volume contribution plus
  the two tissue states.
* **Blood input forcing function (`SUV_BLOOD`).** The heart-VOI whole-blood
  curve used in the original fits is not tabulated in the paper. The blood
  profile used here is **illustrative** (a bi-exponential consistent with the
  reported ~ 7-minute blood half-life), supplied only to demonstrate structural
  behaviour; it is not a digitised reproduction of the authors' input. Absolute
  SUV magnitudes in the figures above are therefore illustrative; the
  cross-over timing and the terminal eigenvalues depend only on the fitted rate
  constants and are reproducible.
* **Printed rate constants vs. stated 11.9 h half-life.** The published rate
  constants (S1/S2 Tables, Figs 3B/4B) give a terminal half-life near 3.6 h for
  both organs, which reproduces the measured 0-195 min window but not the
  abstract's 11.9 h or the 72-hour extrapolations (Figs 3D/4D). The discrepancy
  arises because those extrapolations are driven by a slowly-declining
  whole-body blood tail extending far beyond the 195-minute scan, which is not
  reported and is not part of the four-parameter tissue model. The packaged
  models encode the published, source-traced rate constants as-fitted; they are
  not tuned to the extrapolated half-life.
* **No IIV / residual error.** The paper reports no between-subject random
  effects and no residual-error model for the compartmental fit (weighted least
  squares over two animals). A nominal fixed `propSd = 0.1` is supplied only so
  each model carries a valid residual endpoint for simulation; it is not a
  fitted value. Use `zeroRe()` for typical-value solves, as above.
